title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Bone pain.

HPI
Pt is a 67-year-old male with known carcinoma of the right lung. Pt is currently receiving chemotherapy for the primary site. Pt presents today c/o increased aching and discomfort in the lower spine and ribs. Pt reports the cancer is metastatic to bone. Pain is dull, constant, and rated 7/10. No acute trauma reported.

Medication List
- Chemotherapy (current cycle)
- Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN
- Gabapentin 300mg TID

Exam
Gen: Pt appears in mild distress due to pain.
Vitals: BP 132/84, HR 78, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 96% RA.
Resp: CTAB.
MSK: Tenderness noted over lumbar spine and posterior ribs. No deformity noted.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.

Assessment
1. Carcinoma of the right lung, currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Bone metastases.

Plan
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen as scheduled.
2. Manage bone pain with increased dosage of gabapentin; pt to monitor for sedation.
3. F/u in 2 weeks to assess pain control and tolerance to meds.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the right lung under current treatment is a current malignancy: C34.91.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
The note documents the right lung: use the right-lung code.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
